app.lema: Padel, tennis and football courts by the hour. A portfolio project by Brad López, open source.

portada.subtitulo: Padel, tennis and football in Madrid. Pick a day, see the free hours and book in two clicks.
portada.sinPistasTexto: Try another filter or look at every court.
portada.carrera: Fifty people press Book at the same time on the last free hour. One gets the court. The other forty-nine know it instantly and see the slot as taken. This app exists to show how that is built, and the test that proves it runs against a real database.

comoFunciona.entradilla: Booking a court takes less than a minute.

pasos.texto: Padel, tennis or football. Every court shows its opening hours and how long each slot lasts.
Free and taken hours, in Madrid time. You can book from today onwards.
You need an account. If someone books the same hour an instant before you, you will see it right away and can pick another.
They all appear in My bookings. You can cancel up to two hours before the start.

faq.r: No. It is a demo application: there are no payments or fees, and bookings do not give access to any real court.

faq.p: Can I book more than one hour?
faq.r: Yes. Each booking is one slot; book the next one the same way as the first.

faq.p: What happens if two people book at the same time?
faq.r: Only one gets the hour. The other is told instantly and the slot appears as taken.

faq.p: Which time zone are the slots in?
faq.r: Always Madrid time, where the courts are, even if you check from somewhere else.

normas.entradilla: What you can do with a booking and until when.

lista.texto: Every court has its own opening hours and slot length. Both appear on its page and in the court list.
You can book from today onwards, with no limit on days. A slot that has already started cannot be booked.
Up to two hours before the start. The booking stays in your history as cancelled and the hour becomes free for everyone else.
One account per email, with a password of at least ten characters. From Settings you can change it or sign out on every device.
This is a demo application. There are no payments and bookings do not give access to any real facility. Test data may be deleted at any time.

sobre.entradilla: A booking app built to answer one concrete question: what happens when fifty people press Book at the same time on the last free hour.

demuestra.titulo: A court is never sold twice
demuestra.texto: Fifty simultaneous bookings of the same slot against a real PostgreSQL: exactly one wins. Three different strategies pass the same test.
Opaque token in an httpOnly cookie, hashed in the database, rotated on every login, sliding expiry and an attempt limit.
The Zod schemas the API validates with are the same ones the browser uses to validate the responses.

sobre.carreraA: The test fires fifty requests at once for the last free slot. Only one gets the booking; the other forty-nine get
sobre.carreraB: . The same test runs against three ways of resolving the conflict: a pessimistic lock on the court row, an optimistic version per court and day, and an
sobre.carreraC: constraint in the database itself. Production uses the third one, because it keeps working even if someone adds another route that inserts bookings tomorrow.

sobre.conQueTexto: A pnpm monorepo: a hexagonal API with one module per feature, a React web app with each screen's logic in a hook, and a contracts package shared by both. The code, the tests, the architecture decisions and the instructions to run it locally are in the repository.
